- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are falling, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid premature bottoming.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below prior peak for 3–7 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-period, model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” correction: reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence; if below, increase by 0.5–1.0% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates true volatility; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.33–0.67 range with no clear trend, model tends to overfit short-term noise; use 3-day moving average to smooth forecast.
